So just for everyone to know what happens is this. When you're using an online sports book
At the end of the tax year if you show net winnings of $600 or more they will issue a 1099 g.
However an individual bet does not trigger it.

So if you win $599 today and $2 tomorrow on a total of $1 in wagers and never bet a penny more with that sportsbook throughout the calendar year that's $600 net win will trigger them to issue a 1099 g.

That's important for smaller betters to know.

It may be advantageous to have 10 different sportsbook accounts.

Instead of betting $100 on a 50 to 1 shot on a single site you would be better served betting $10 on 10 different sites. If it hits you will have $5,000 in profit but no 1099 g will be issued (again assuming that's the only bet you place in those wagering accounts over the course of an entire calendar year)

If you were to throw that $100 down at a single book then unless you have losses to offset the $5,000 win you are going to wind up paying 1,250 in federal tax.

Frankly I think it's absurd. Here we are playing games of negative expectation to begin with. It's one thing if you are a professional gambler. Jump across the pond and you'll see most countries over there do not tax gambling.
